extracted.intended_audience: criminalists, judges, courtroom examiners, forensic/legal professionals assessing female defendants and witnesses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for criminal-justice practitioners on interpreting testimony, motives, and behaviour of women (defendants, witnesses, and accomplices) in criminal cases; emphasizes psychological/behavioral signs, social causes, and investigative leads beyond statutory analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty versus lying (definition of dishonesty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to be honest, and to lie, are two different things; the dishonest person does not tell the truth, the liar tells the untruth. It is dishonest to suppress a portion of the truth, to lead others into mistakes, to fail to justify appearances, and to make use of appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat suppression, concealment, and misuse of appearances as forms of dishonesty distinct from direct lying; these can create more confusion and are often harder to detect than explicit falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty more dangerous and harder to uncover
rubrics_metrics.description: The dishonest person may not have said a single untrue word and still have introduced many more difficulties, confusions and deceptions than the liar. He is for this reason more dangerous than the latter. Also, because his conduct is more difficult to uncover and because he is more difficult to conquer than the liar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize detection of omissions and misleading presentation; do not equate absence of explicit lies with veracity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social causes of feminine dishonesty and courtroom handling
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be a mistake to deal too sternly in court with the dishonesty of women, for we ourselves and social conditions are responsible for much of it... we compel them to be dishonest by our round-about handling of every ticklish subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prudery and indirect questioning; use simple, absolutely open discussion to reduce compelled dishonesty. Courtesy is required, but frankness often elicits more truthful responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deception by appearance and suppression rather than direct lying
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of deception or concealment depends on dishonesty rather than on pure deceit, because it consists much more in the use of whatever is at hand, and in suppression of material, than on direct lies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for selective presentation and use of appearances; probe for omitted facts rather than only searching for contradicted statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonverbal/expressive signs in female deception
rubrics_metrics.description: The play of features, the eyes, the breast, the attitude, betrays almost always even the experienced female offender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to facial micro-expressions, posture and affective displays as possible reveals of concealed material, recognizing cultural and individual variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences in confession behavior between men and women
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man once confesses, he confesses with less constraint than a woman, and he is less likely, even if he is very bad, to take advantage of false favorable appearances, while woman accepts them with the semblance of innocence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect greater reluctance and guardedness in female confessions; absence of a full confession from a woman may reflect different strategic or socialized responses rather than absence of culpability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret yes/no answers and limits carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Even her simplest affirmation or denial is not honest. Her 'no' is not definite... the woman says 'yes' and 'no,' even when only a small portion of one or the other asserts a truth behind which she can hide herself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When receiving categorical replies, probe for qualifications and partial truths; do not accept simple yes/no at face value—seek the portion of truth supporting the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tears: distinguish voluntary/auto-suggested tears from genuine pain
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories in novels... are fairy tales; in point of fact... Some tiny reason, a little time, a little auto-suggestion, and a little imagination,--these can keep every woman weeping eternally... Beware, however, of the silent tears of real pain, especially of hurt innocence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess tears by context, duration, provocation, and suppression attempts; silent, suppressed tears may indicate real pain/innocence, whereas quick manufactured crying may be a rhetorical device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fainting: often exaggerated or induced; treat with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater number of fainting fits are either altogether false, or something between fainting and wakefulness... If only a little exaggeration, auto-suggestion, relaxation, and the attempt to dodge the unpleasant circumstance are added, then the fainting fit is ready to order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not automatically treat fainting as genuine; consider physiological signs and context before allowing it to influence judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promises from women are unreliable for secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a criminalist permits a woman to promise not to tell anybody else of her testimony... The criminalist must not accept promises at all, and he is only getting his reward when women fool him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on assurances or promises of confidentiality from witnesses/defendants—use formal protections and corroboration instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited legal/regulatory comprehension risk in women witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Women, moreover, do not understand the least regulation... even intelligent women could not see why it was wrong to make a 'small' change in a public register... why the dog must be kept chained; and what good such 'vexations' could do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testimony involves understanding of regulations or legal boundaries, assess whether ignorance—not malice—is responsible; explain and probe factual understanding rather than assuming willful misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective sense of private property leading to petty theft
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in their own homes women do not conceive property too rigidly. They appropriate pen, paper, pencils, clothes, etc., without having any idea of replacing what they have taken away... this defective property-sense is most clearly shown in the notorious fact that women cheat at cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate cultural/domestic norms around sharing from criminal intent; examine escalation from petty appropriations to more serious theft in light of opportunity and need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propensity for small-scale theft and cheating as an investigative indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: We find many women among swindlers, gamblers, and counterfeiters... the cleverest and most useful servants are frequently thievish... the defect in the sense of property with regard to little things explains how many a woman became a criminal--the road she wandered on grew, step by step, more extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate history of petty dishonest acts as a potential pathway to larger property offenses; consider socioeconomic pressures and opportunity as causal factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness bias due to personal culpability or similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: When an honest, well-conducted woman commits petty crimes, she does not consider them as crimes... she tends to excuse her neighbor’s derelictions... when we try to find out from feminine witnesses facts concerning the objects on which we properly lay stress, they do not answer and cause us to make mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect tendency to excuse or minimize behaviour in others that the witness herself has committed; corroborate testimony and probe for definitional differences between moral and legal categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty/disloyalty as crucial evidentiary factor
rubrics_metrics.description: From honesty to loyalty is but a step... the whole problem of evidence takes a different form according to the assumption that this loyalty does, or does not, exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess feminine loyalty carefully—its presence or absence can change inference patterns in homicide, arson, perversion of trust, etc.; look for determinative factors and presentational difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints of neglect as indicator of adulterous inclination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is only a simple and safe method for discovering whether a woman is loyal to her husband--lead her to say whether her husband neglects her. Every woman who complains that her husband neglects her is an adulteress or in the way of becoming one, for she seeks the most thrifty, the really sound reason which would justify adultery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expressions of dissatisfaction and complaints about neglect as investigative leads to probe sexual/marital motives, while not treating them as conclusive proof without corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love and jealousy as potent motives for crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Love is of greater importance in the criminal court than the statutes allow... When a woman commits a crime because of jealousy... we have first of all to do our duty properly, to distinguish the biological difference between the human criminal and the normal human being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor love and jealousy into motive analysis beyond statutory categories; although jealousy is hard to discover, known affairs and relational evidence can help infer its degree and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jealousy inferred from known affair rather than direct proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Jealousy is rare to discover and unreliable, while her love-affair is known to everybody. Once this becomes an established fact, we can determine also the degree of her jealousy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an affair is established, infer jealousy as a plausible motive and evaluate its likely intensity from circumstantial indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complicity through devotion: 'complete surrender' as explanation for aiding criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: What nature demands of woman is complete surrender to man... If a woman once depends on a man she follows him everywhere, and even if he commits the most disgusting crimes she helps him and is his loyalest comrade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that romantic devotion can produce willing or unreflective complicity; investigate relational dynamics when assessing accomplice liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance of maltreatment explained by feminine love
rubrics_metrics.description: For the same reason women often bear interminably long maltreatment at the hands of their husbands or lovers... the whole thing is explained if the motive was really feminine love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret prolonged submissive behaviour or failure to flee/mutual assistance in light of attachment and dependency rather than purely rational choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about platonic friendships between sexes; test for sexual motives
rubrics_metrics.description: There are friendships between men and women, although such friendships are very rare... The necessary thing in treating these cases is caution, for it will be impossible to prove these friendships unlikely, and hence unjust to deny them without further evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a defendant or witness claims a cross-sex friendship, probe whether sexual interest can be excluded; do not dismiss claims out of hand but require evidence to support them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Female friendships and group solidarity bias in testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Friendship between women is popularly little valued... Envy, dislike, jealousy, and egoism play up vividly, and he is a successful judge who can discover how much of the evidence is born of these motives... just as soon as we expressly or tacitly suggest common feminine qualities, or start to speak of some matter in which the witness herself feels guilty, she turns about and defends where before she had been attacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep examination concrete to avoid triggering generalized, protective responses among women witnesses; watch for shifts from concrete to general that indicate solidarity or defensive bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feminine hatred, revenge and intensity of motive
rubrics_metrics.description: Feminine hatred is much intenser than masculine hatred... a woman seeking revenge is capable of anything... When some crime with revenge as motive is before us, and we have no way of getting at the criminal, our first suspicion should be directed toward a woman or an effeminate man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat revenge motive as potentially more extreme and long-delayed in women; include women prominently in suspect lists where vengeance is plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Female cruelty linked to weakness and defensive motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Feminine cruelty is directly connected with feminine anger and hatred... Perhaps it would be proper to conceive this cruelty as a form of defence, or the expression of defence... many a curious bit of feminine cruelty is due to feminine traits misunderstood, suppressed, but in themselves good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When encountering seemingly cruel acts by women, consider defensive, resource-protective, or child-rearing rationales rather than assuming purely sadistic intent; examine socio-economic context (e.g., scarcity, frugality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dispositional and contextual traits to explain crime and identify suspects
rubrics_metrics.description: These facts serve not only to explain the crime, but to reveal the criminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate behavioral, relational, and social-contextual observations (love, jealousy, dishonesty, loyalty, cruelty) into investigative reasoning rather than relying solely on statutory categories.
